queries.question: List all distinct banks (LEI_Code, Name, Country) from the metadata table.
notes: Note: Confirms the bank universe (name, country) the rest of the project is built on.
queries.sql:
select distinct metadata.lei_code, metadata.name, metadata.country,
       metadata.desc_country, credit.nsa
from metadata
inner join credit on metadata.lei_code = credit.lei_code;

queries.question: Find LEI_Codes in credit that have no match in the metadata table (data quality check).
notes: Note: Found two unmatched LEI_Codes. One was a genuine placeholder row (not a real bank). The other belonged to a real bank (Banco de Crédito Social Cooperativo, ES) whose LEI_Code had been corrupted in the metadata file — Excel had auto-converted the 20-digit code into scientific notation (9.598E+19). Verified the true value against the credit table and the bank's country/name, then corrected it with an UPDATE. Re-running the check afterward left only the genuine placeholder row.
queries.sql:
select distinct c.lei_code
from credit as c
left join metadata as m on c.lei_code = m.lei_code
where m.lei_code is null;

queries.question: List the distinct Item/Label combinations available, and pick one to anchor the analysis on.
notes: Note: Found 89 distinct Item/Label combinations spanning several EBA templates. Chose three related items as the main anchors: 2520502 (Original Exposure), 2520522 (Exposure value), 2520532 (Risk exposure amount) — all 'by exposure class' versions. These were chosen because they exist in both the STA and IRB report types; the plain, non-broken-down totals only exist under STA and would silently exclude every IRB bank.

queries.question: For the latest period, what is the total credit exposure across all banks, for each anchor item?
notes: Run once per anchor item: replace 2520502 with 2520522 and 2520532 (the three measures are not additive).

Note: Run once per item (2520502, 2520522, 2520532). The three totals are not directly comparable — Original Exposure (gross) is larger than Exposure value (post credit-risk mitigation), which is larger again than Risk exposure amount (post risk-weighting). Each should be read on its own, not summed together.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: Totals at June 2025: original exposure EUR 31.3tn, exposure value EUR 26.3tn, risk exposure amount EUR 7.9tn.
queries.sql:
select item, label, sum(amount) as total_credit_exposure
from credit
where period = '202506'
and item = '2520502' and country = 0
group by item, label;

queries.question: How many distinct banks reported each anchor item in the latest period?
notes: Anchor item shown is 2520502; repeat with 2520522 and 2520532 for the other two measures.

Note: LEI 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' is the EBA's "All other banks" aggregate, not a bank. Bank-level measures exclude it (queries that join bank_metadata drop it automatically, because the metadata file stores the code in lower case).
queries.result: The "All other banks" aggregate (LEI XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) is excluded from bank-level counts and rankings; it is not a single bank. 119 banks reported original exposure at June 2025.
queries.sql:
select count(distinct lei_code)
from credit
where period = '202506'
and item = '2520502' and lei_code <> 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX';

queries.question: What is the average exposure per bank, for each anchor item?
notes: Anchor item shown is 2520502; repeat with 2520522 and 2520532 for the other two measures.

Note: The question is ambiguous as worded — it could mean the average size of a single reported row, or the average size of a bank's whole book. Went with the second, more meaningful interpretation: total exposure divided by the number of distinct banks.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.

Note: LEI 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' is the EBA's "All other banks" aggregate, not a bank. Bank-level measures exclude it (queries that join bank_metadata drop it automatically, because the metadata file stores the code in lower case).
queries.result: Average per bank: original exposure EUR 259bn, exposure value EUR 217bn, risk exposure amount EUR 65bn.
queries.sql:
select item, label, sum(amount)/count(distinct lei_code) as avg_exposure_per_bank
from credit
where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0 and lei_code <> 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'
group by item, label;

queries.question: What are the top 20 largest single exposure rows (bank + country + sector combination)?
notes: Anchor item shown is 2520502; repeat with 2520522 and 2520532 for the other two measures.

Note: These rows are dominated by single large, concentrated exposures (one bank's exposure to one country/sector) — not by overall bank size. A bank with a large but well-spread book across many rows won't appear here even if its total exposure is far bigger, because no single row captures its full size. Useful for spotting concentrated single bets, not for ranking the biggest banks overall (that's Q8).

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: The largest rows are BNP Paribas (EUR 865bn), Crédit Agricole (EUR 740bn) and ING (EUR 669bn); the top 20 rows belong to ten of the largest banking groups. A bank with a large book spread across many classes can be absent here, so this ranks concentrated positions, not bank size (Q8, Q18).
queries.sql:
select metadata.name, credit.lei_code, credit.item, credit.exposure, credit.amount
from credit
inner join metadata on metadata.lei_code = credit.lei_code
where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and credit.country = 0
order by amount desc
limit 20;

queries.question: What % of total exposure do the top 20 banks represent? (concentration risk)
notes: Anchor item shown is 2520502; repeat with 2520522 and 2520532 for the other two measures.
Note: Top 20 banks' Original Exposure as a % of total portfolio. Built using CTEs: bank-level totals, top-20 sum, grand total, then divided.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.

Note: LEI 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' is the EBA's "All other banks" aggregate, not a bank. Bank-level measures exclude it (queries that join bank_metadata drop it automatically, because the metadata file stores the code in lower case).
queries.result: The top 20 banks hold 66.4% of original exposure held by named banks.
queries.sql:
with exp_by_bank as (
    select lei_code, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0 and lei_code <> 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'
    group by lei_code
),
top20 as (
    select sum(total) as top20total
    from (
        select lei_code, total
        from exp_by_bank
        order by total desc
        limit 20
    ) as t
),
all_total as (
    select sum(total) as alltotal
    from exp_by_bank
)
select top20.top20total, all_total.alltotal,
       top20.top20total / all_total.alltotal * 100 as pertop20
from top20, all_total;

queries.question: What is total exposure by NSA (bank home country)?
notes: Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.sql:
select nsa, sum(amount) as total_exposure
from credit
where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0
group by nsa;

queries.question: Which 10 countries have the largest exposures?
notes: Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.sql:
select nsa, sum(amount) as total_exposure
from credit
where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0
group by nsa
order by total_exposure desc
limit 10;

queries.question: Which countries account for more than 5% of total exposure?
notes: Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.sql:
with exp_by_nsa as (
    select nsa, sum(amount) as total_exposure
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0
    group by nsa
)
select exp_by_nsa.nsa, exp_by_nsa.total_exposure
from exp_by_nsa
where exp_by_nsa.total_exposure > (
    select 0.05 * sum(total_exposure)
    from exp_by_nsa
);

queries.question: What % of total exposure does each country represent?
notes: Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: Shares by bank home country: France 28.9%, Germany 15.4%, Spain 13.7%, Italy 10.5%, Netherlands 9.2%. Five countries are above 5% (Q11) and together hold 77.7%.
queries.sql:
with exp_by_nsa as (
    select nsa, sum(amount) as total_exposure
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0
    group by nsa
),
alltotal as (
    select sum(total_exposure) as alltotal
    from exp_by_nsa
)
select exp_by_nsa.nsa, exp_by_nsa.total_exposure,
       exp_by_nsa.total_exposure / alltotal.alltotal * 100 as per_exp
from exp_by_nsa, alltotal;

queries.question: What is total exposure by NACE sector code?
notes: Note: Initial finding claimed nace_codes = 0 ('No breakdown') meant ~50% of exposure was unclassified. This was later found to be wrong — see the correction below.

Correction: item 2521301 repeats every bank-sector pair under Perf_Status 0 (total), 2, 4 and 5. Filtering on pref_status = 0 avoids counting the same exposure more than once (the first draft omitted it).
queries.sql:
select item, credit.label, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, sum(amount) as total_exposure
from credit
inner join nace_metadata on credit.nace_codes = nace_metadata.nace_codes
where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.nace_codes != '0' and credit.pref_status = 0
group by item, credit.label, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
order by item;

queries.question: Correction: is nace_codes = 0 really unclassified exposure?
notes: Note: Checked each bank's nace_codes = 0 total against the sum of its 19 real sector rows — they matched almost exactly. This means nace_codes = 0 is a duplicate total, not unclassified exposure. Sector analysis should exclude nace_codes = 0. The original Q13 totals (using only the 19 real sectors) were correct all along.
queries.sql:
with bybank as (
    select item, nace_codes, lei_code, sum(amount) as totalnace0
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and nace_codes = '0'
    group by item, nace_codes, lei_code
),
bybanknace as (
    select item, lei_code, sum(amount) as totalallnace
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and nace_codes != '0'
    group by item, lei_code
)
select bybank.item, bybank.lei_code, totalnace0, totalallnace
from bybank
inner join bybanknace on bybank.item = bybanknace.item and bybank.lei_code = bybanknace.lei_code
order by bybank.item;

queries.question: Within each NACE sector, what % of total exposure does each bank represent?
notes: Correction: item 2521301 repeats every bank-sector pair under Perf_Status 0 (total), 2, 4 and 5. Filtering on pref_status = 0 avoids counting the same exposure more than once (the first draft omitted it).
queries.sql:
with bybankbysector as (
    select item, lei_code, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.nace_codes != '0' and credit.pref_status = 0
    group by item, lei_code, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
),
bysector as (
    select item, nace_codes, label, sum(total) as total
    from bybankbysector
    group by item, nace_codes, label
)
select bybankbysector.item, bybankbysector.lei_code, bybankbysector.nace_codes, bybankbysector.label,
       bybankbysector.total, bysector.total,
       bybankbysector.total / nullif(bysector.total, 0) * 100 as bybankbysectorconc
from bybankbysector
inner join bysector
    on bysector.item = bybankbysector.item and bysector.nace_codes = bybankbysector.nace_codes
order by bybankbysector.item, bybankbysector.nace_codes;

queries.question: Which NACE sectors have the highest average exposure size?
notes: Note: Average exposure size per sector closely tracks Q13's total-exposure ranking — Real Estate leads both, followed by Manufacturing and Wholesale/Retail Trade. No sector shows an unusually high average relative to its total rank, meaning exposure size scales fairly evenly with the number of reporting banks — no sign of a small group of banks making unusually large, concentrated bets in any one sector.

Correction: item 2521301 repeats every bank-sector pair under Perf_Status 0 (total), 2, 4 and 5. Filtering on pref_status = 0 avoids counting the same exposure more than once (the first draft omitted it).
queries.sql:
with bybankbysector as (
    select item, lei_code, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.nace_codes != '0' and credit.pref_status = 0
    group by item, lei_code, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
),
bysector as (
    select item, nace_codes, label, sum(total) as total
    from bybankbysector
    group by item, nace_codes, label
)
select bysector.item, bysector.nace_codes, bysector.label, bysector.total,
       bysector.total / count(distinct bybankbysector.lei_code) as avgbysector
from bysector
inner join bybankbysector
    on bybankbysector.item = bysector.item and bybankbysector.nace_codes = bysector.nace_codes
group by bysector.item, bysector.nace_codes, bysector.label, bysector.total
order by bysector.item, avgbysector desc;

queries.question: Which sectors represent more than 10% of portfolio exposure?
notes: Note: Real Estate, Manufacturing, and Wholesale/Retail Trade are consistently the three sectors exceeding 10% of exposure, together representing roughly half the classified portfolio — a genuine sector concentration. Separately, under item 2521303 (fair-value losses on non-performing exposure), Real Estate alone accounts for ~47% — nearly double its ~25% share of gross exposure — suggesting Real Estate exposures are disproportionately represented among distressed exposure relative to their overall size.

Correction: item 2521301 repeats every bank-sector pair under Perf_Status 0 (total), 2, 4 and 5. Filtering on pref_status = 0 avoids counting the same exposure more than once (the first draft omitted it).
queries.result: Real Estate (25.5%), Manufacturing (15.1%) and Wholesale and retail trade (12.9%) each exceed 10% of gross carrying amount and together make up about 53% of the classified portfolio.
queries.sql:
with bysector as (
    select item, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, sum(amount) as sectortotal
    from credit
    inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.nace_codes != '0' and credit.pref_status = 0
    group by item, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
),
itemtotal as (
    select item, sum(sectortotal) as itemtotal
    from bysector
    group by item
)
select item, nace_codes, label, sectorconc
from (
    select bysector.item, nace_codes, label, sectortotal, itemtotal,
           sectortotal / itemtotal * 100 as sectorconc
    from bysector
    inner join itemtotal on itemtotal.item = bysector.item
) as t
where sectorconc >= 10;

queries.question: Which sectors hold the largest share of accumulated fair-value losses on non-performing exposure?
notes: Added to make the Real Estate finding in Q16 reproducible (item 2521303 is reported by sector only, no status split).
queries.result: Real Estate: 47.1% of the total.
queries.sql:
with bysector as (
    select item, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, sum(amount) as sectortotal
    from credit
    inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521303' and credit.nace_codes != 0
    group by item, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
)
select item, nace_codes, label, sectortotal,
       sectortotal / sum(sectortotal) over () * 100 as sector_share_pct
from bysector
order by sector_share_pct desc;

queries.question: Which banks have exposure above the overall average?
notes: Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: Banks above the average: 27 for original exposure, 28 for exposure value and 28 for risk exposure amount, out of 119.
queries.sql:
with bybank as (
    select item, credit.lei_code, name, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = credit.lei_code
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2520502', '2520522', '2520532') and credit.country = 0
    group by item, credit.lei_code, name
),
byitem as (
    select item, sum(total) as total, sum(total) / count(distinct lei_code) as avg
    from bybank
    group by item
)
select bybank.item, lei_code, name, byitem.avg, bybank.total
from bybank
inner join byitem on byitem.item = bybank.item
where bybank.total >= byitem.avg
order by bybank.item, byitem.avg desc;

queries.question: Which banks cumulatively account for 50% of total exposure?
notes: Note: Roughly 10-12 banks (out of ~120) account for half of total reported exposure, across all three anchor items — confirming the concentration pattern already seen in Q8, now found independently using a running total instead of a fixed top-20 cutoff.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: Half of total exposure is held by 11 banks on original exposure, 13 on exposure value and 11 on risk exposure amount, out of 119.
queries.sql:
with bybank as (
    select item, credit.lei_code, name, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = credit.lei_code
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2520502', '2520522', '2520532') and credit.country = 0
    group by item, credit.lei_code, name
),
byitem as (
    select item, sum(total) as total, sum(total) / 2 as half
    from bybank
    group by item
),
byrunningsum as (
    select bybank.item, lei_code, name, bybank.total, half,
           sum(bybank.total) over (partition by bybank.item order by bybank.total desc) as running_sum
    from bybank
    inner join byitem on byitem.item = bybank.item
    group by bybank.item, lei_code, name, bybank.total, half
),
byrn as (
    select *, row_number() over (partition by item order by running_sum) as rn
    from byrunningsum
    where running_sum >= half
),
byrn1 as (
    select item, running_sum
    from byrn
    where rn = 1
)
select byrunningsum.item, lei_code, name, total, half, byrunningsum.running_sum
from byrunningsum
join byrn1 on byrn1.item = byrunningsum.item
where byrunningsum.running_sum <= byrn1.running_sum;

queries.question: Distribution of banks by exposure-size bucket (<€1bn, €1–10bn, €10–100bn, €100bn–1tri, >1tri).
notes: Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: Original exposure: 3 banks below EUR 10bn, 62 between EUR 10bn and 100bn, 45 between EUR 100bn and 1tn, and 9 above EUR 1tn.
queries.sql:
with bybank as (
    select item, credit.lei_code, name, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = credit.lei_code
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2520502', '2520522', '2520532') and credit.country = 0
    group by item, credit.lei_code, name
),
bybucket as (
    select item, lei_code, name, total,
        case
            when total < 1000 then '< 1bn'
            when total < 10000 then '1bn to <10 bn'
            when total < 100000 then '10 bn to <100 bn'
            when total < 1000000 then '100 bn to <1 tri'
            else '>= 1 tri'
        end as exposure_bucket
    from bybank
)
select item, exposure_bucket, count(lei_code) as count
from bybucket
group by item, exposure_bucket
order by item,
    case exposure_bucket
        when '< 1bn' then 1
        when '1bn to <10 bn' then 2
        when '10 bn to <100 bn' then 3
        when '100 bn to <1 tri' then 4
        when '>= 1 tri' then 5
    end;

queries.question: What is total exposure split by Perf_Status (performing vs non-performing), including the full sub-category breakdown?
notes: Note: Of the 7 non-zero codes returned, only 1 (Performing) and 2 (Non Performing) are the true top- level, non-overlapping split. Codes 3, 4, 12, 23, and 222 are sub-categories nested inside 1 or 2 — summing all 7 together would double-count. Full breakdown shown for detail; the clean total is 1 + 2 only. Two related items (2520605, by exposure class; 2521301, the NACE item) were checked and found to be different, non-substitutable scopes — 2521301 turned out to be the better anchor for the sector-level breakdown in Q22.
queries.sql:
select item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, sum(amount) as total_exposure
from credit
inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and credit.pref_status != 0
group by item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label;

queries.question: Same breakdown, by country.
queries.sql:
select item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, nsa, sum(amount) as total_exposure
from credit
inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and credit.pref_status != 0
group by item, credit.label, nsa, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label
order by credit.pref_status asc, total_exposure desc;

queries.question: Which NSA country has the highest non-performing exposure amount?
queries.sql:
select item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, nsa, sum(amount) as highest_exposure
from credit
inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and credit.pref_status = 2
group by item, credit.label, nsa, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label
order by highest_exposure desc
limit 1;

queries.question: What is non-performing exposure by sector, including all Perf_Status sub-categories?
queries.sql:
select item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label,
       sum(amount) as highest_exposure
from credit
inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.pref_status != 0 and credit.nace_codes != 0
group by item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
order by credit.pref_status asc, credit.nace_codes asc, highest_exposure desc;

queries.question: Which NACE sectors carry the largest non-performing exposure amount?
queries.sql:
select item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label,
       sum(amount) as highest_exposure
from credit
inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.pref_status = 2 and credit.nace_codes != 0
group by item, credit.label, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
order by highest_exposure desc;

queries.question: Which NACE sectors have the highest non-performing exposure rate (non-performing ÷ sector total), rather than the highest raw amount?
notes: Note: Ranking sectors by non-performing rate tells a different story than Q22a: Construction has the highest NPE rate (6.4%), more than double Real Estate's (2.8%), despite Real Estate having a far larger absolute non-performing amount. Construction loans are proportionally riskier — a smaller sector, but a higher share of its lending has gone bad. Real Estate's top ranking in Q22a mainly reflects its overall size, not elevated risk per loan.

Correction: item 2521301 repeats every bank-sector pair under Perf_Status 0 (total), 2, 4 and 5. Filtering on pref_status = 0 avoids counting the same exposure more than once (the first draft omitted it).
queries.result: Construction has the highest NPE rate (6.4%), followed by Accommodation and food service (5.6%) and Wholesale and retail trade (4.2%).
queries.sql:
with sector_total as (
    select credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, sum(amount) as total_pref_status
    from credit
    inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = credit.nace_codes
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and credit.nace_codes != '0'
      and credit.pref_status = 0
    group by credit.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label
),
sector_npe as (
    select nace_codes, sum(amount) as total_pref_status2
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and nace_codes != '0' and pref_status = '2'
    group by nace_codes
)
select sector_total.nace_codes, sector_total.label, sector_total.total_pref_status, sector_npe.total_pref_status2,
       sector_npe.total_pref_status2 / sector_total.total_pref_status * 100 as npe_rate_pct
from sector_total
inner join sector_npe on sector_npe.nace_codes = sector_total.nace_codes
order by npe_rate_pct desc;

queries.question: What % of total portfolio exposure is non-performing vs performing? (board-level KPI)
notes: Note: Non-performing ratio = 2.14% of total exposure (Performing + Non Performing, codes 1+2 only). This is consistent with typical EU bank NPL ratios (roughly 1-3%), confirming the calculation is realistic.
queries.sql:
with by_prefstatus as (
    select item, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, sum(amount) as total
    from credit
    inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and credit.pref_status in ('1', '2')
    group by item, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label
),
total as (
    select item, sum(total) as total_exposure
    from by_prefstatus
    group by item
)
select by_prefstatus.item, pref_status, label, total, total_exposure,
       total / total_exposure * 100 as exp_pct
from by_prefstatus
inner join total on total.item = by_prefstatus.item;

queries.question: How much accumulated impairment does each sector carry relative to its gross carrying amount?
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn | Item(s): 2521301 (gross carrying amount), 2521302 (accumulated impairment)
notes: Impairment ratio = accumulated impairment / gross carrying amount (all loans in the sector). The NACE template does not split impairment by performing status, so a sector-level NPE coverage ratio cannot be built from it.
queries.result: Construction has the highest ratio (4.1%), followed by Accommodation and food service (3.5%) and Wholesale and retail trade (2.8%). Real Estate is 1.4%. Construction is highest on both the NPE rate (Q22b) and the impairment ratio.
queries.sql:
with gross as (
    select nace_codes, sum(amount) as gross_amt
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and pref_status = 0 and nace_codes != 0
    group by nace_codes
),
imp as (
    select nace_codes, sum(amount) as impairment
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521302' and nace_codes != 0
    group by nace_codes
)
select gross.nace_codes, nace_metadata.label, gross.gross_amt, imp.impairment,
       imp.impairment / nullif(gross.gross_amt, 0) * 100 as impairment_ratio_pct
from gross
inner join imp on imp.nace_codes = gross.nace_codes
inner join nace_metadata on nace_metadata.nace_codes = gross.nace_codes
order by impairment_ratio_pct desc;

queries.question: How well are non-performing loans covered by provisions, by bank home country?
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn | Item(s): 2520603 (gross carrying amount), 2520613 (impairment and provisions)
notes: NPE coverage = provisions on non-performing loans / gross non-performing loans (Perf_Status 2). Computed from summed amounts, so larger banks weigh more (a ratio of sums, not an average of bank ratios).
queries.result: Among the large markets: Italy 52.1%, Spain 45.5%, France 44.4%, Germany 35.0%, Netherlands 24.2%. Across all 26 countries the range runs from 19.6% (Estonia) to 61.3% (Hungary). Low coverage combined with a large NPE stock means more capital impact when NPEs rise, which is the mechanism the stress-test model captures.
queries.sql:
with npe as (
    select nsa,
           sum(case when item = '2520603' then amount end) as gross_npe,
           sum(case when item = '2520613' then amount end) as provision_npe
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2520603', '2520613') and pref_status = 2
    group by nsa
)
select nsa, gross_npe, provision_npe,
       provision_npe / nullif(gross_npe, 0) * 100 as npe_coverage_pct
from npe
order by gross_npe desc;

queries.question: Which banks report the most risk-weighted books relative to their size? (RWA density)
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn | Item(s): 2520532 (risk exposure amount), 2520522 (exposure value)
notes: RWA density = credit-risk risk exposure amount / exposure value, both "by exposure class (SA and IRB)". Public-sector funding agencies show near-zero density (Kommuninvest 0.03%, SFIL 3.6%, Nederlandse Waterschapsbank 4.2%, Kuntarahoitus 1.5%) because their lending is government-backed. Exposure value is gross of provisions for IRB, so density is comparable across banks but not to leverage-ratio exposure.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.
queries.result: Median 31.2% across 119 banks. Highest: Bpifrance 76.3% and Volkswagen Financial Services 74.5%. Examples among the stress-model banks: Santander 33.9%, BNP Paribas 35.4%, BAWAG 28.8%, CEC Bank 23.5%.
queries.sql:
with bybank as (
    select lei_code,
           sum(case when item = '2520532' then amount end) as rea,
           sum(case when item = '2520522' then amount end) as exposure_value
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2520532', '2520522') and country = 0
    group by lei_code
)
select bank_metadata.name, bank_metadata.country, bybank.exposure_value, bybank.rea,
       bybank.rea / nullif(bybank.exposure_value, 0) * 100 as rwa_density_pct
from bybank
inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = bybank.lei_code
where bybank.exposure_value > 0
order by rwa_density_pct desc;

queries.question: How concentrated is exposure by bank, by country and by sector? (Herfindahl-Hirschman index)
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn | Item(s): 2520502 (banks, countries), 2521301 (sectors)
notes: HHI = sum of squared percentage shares, 0 to 10,000. Common reading: under 1,500 unconcentrated, above 2,500 highly concentrated. Also reports the effective number of equal-sized units (10,000 / HHI).

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.

Note: LEI 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' is the EBA's "All other banks" aggregate, not a bank. Bank-level measures exclude it (queries that join bank_metadata drop it automatically, because the metadata file stores the code in lower case).
queries.result:
Dimension  Units  HHI    Effective number of equal-sized units
   ---------  -----  -----  -------------------------------------
   Bank       119    302    33.1
   Country    26     1,501  6.7
   Sector     19     1,234  8.1

By bank (excluding the "All other banks" aggregate), exposure is not concentrated in the HHI sense, even though 11 banks hold half of it (Q18), because the large banks are similar in size. By country it sits at the edge of the "unconcentrated" band (HHI 1,500), with an effective 6.7 countries behind 26.
queries.sql:
with bank as (
    select 'bank' as dimension, lei_code as unit, sum(amount) as amt
    from credit where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0 and lei_code <> 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' group by lei_code
),
country as (
    select 'country', nsa, sum(amount)
    from credit where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0 group by nsa
),
sector as (
    select 'sector', nace_codes::text, sum(amount)
    from credit where period = '202506' and item = '2521301' and pref_status = 0 and nace_codes != 0 group by nace_codes
),
unioned as (
    select * from bank union all select * from country union all select * from sector
),
shares as (
    select dimension, unit, amt, amt / sum(amt) over (partition by dimension) * 100 as share_pct
    from unioned
)
select dimension, count(*) as units,
       round(sum(share_pct * share_pct)::numeric, 0) as hhi,
       round((10000 / sum(share_pct * share_pct))::numeric, 1) as effective_units
from shares
group by dimension
order by dimension;

queries.question: Are concentration and the NPE ratio rising or falling across the four reporting periods?
notes: The number of banks reporting differs by period (115, 119, 110, 119, excluding the "All other banks" aggregate), so period-to-period changes mix real movement with sample changes. A like-for-like comparison would restrict to banks reporting in all four periods.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.

Note: LEI 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' is the EBA's "All other banks" aggregate, not a bank. Bank-level measures exclude it (queries that join bank_metadata drop it automatically, because the metadata file stores the code in lower case).
queries.result:
Period   Banks reporting  Top-20 share  NPE ratio
   -------  ---------------  ------------  ---------
   2024-09  115              67.9%         2.24%
   2024-12  119              67.2%         2.21%
   2025-03  110              69.0%         2.17%
   2025-06  119              66.4%         2.14%

The top-20 share moves with the number of banks reporting (it is highest in the period with the fewest banks), so it is not read as a trend.
queries.sql:
with exposure as (
    select period, lei_code, sum(amount) as amt
    from credit where item = '2520502' and country = 0 and lei_code <> 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' group by period, lei_code
),
ranked as (
    select period, lei_code, amt, row_number() over (partition by period order by amt desc) as rn
    from exposure
),
concentration as (
    select period, count(*) as banks_reporting, sum(amt) as total_exposure,
           sum(case when rn <= 20 then amt end) / sum(amt) * 100 as top20_share_pct
    from ranked group by period
),
npe as (
    select period,
           sum(case when pref_status = 2 then amount end) / sum(amount) * 100 as npe_ratio_pct
    from credit
    where item = '2520603' and pref_status in (1, 2)
    group by period
)
select concentration.period, banks_reporting, total_exposure, top20_share_pct, npe.npe_ratio_pct
from concentration
inner join npe on npe.period = concentration.period
order by concentration.period;

queries.question: Are the banks that drive exposure concentration also the ones with higher NPE ratios?
notes: Splits banks into the 11 largest (about half of all exposure, see Q18) and the rest, and compares the pooled NPE ratio of each group. Also reports the correlation between log exposure size and bank NPE ratio.

Correction: items 2520502, 2520522 and 2520532 hold a total row per bank and exposure class (counterparty country = 0) plus a breakdown of the same exposure by the bank's top counterparty countries (country <> 0). Summing all rows counts that exposure about twice, so this query keeps country = 0 only.

Note: LEI 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' is the EBA's "All other banks" aggregate, not a bank. Bank-level measures exclude it (queries that join bank_metadata drop it automatically, because the metadata file stores the code in lower case).
queries.result: The 11 largest banks have a pooled NPE ratio of 2.47%, against 1.81% for the other 96 banks. Across individual banks, the correlation between log exposure size and NPE ratio is close to zero (−0.03). The higher pooled figure for the largest banks comes from a few large banks with high NPE ratios, not from a general link between size and risk.
queries.sql:
with exposure as (
    select lei_code, sum(amount) as exposure
    from credit where period = '202506' and item = '2520502' and country = 0 and lei_code <> 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' group by lei_code
),
loans as (
    select lei_code,
           sum(amount) as loans_gross,
           sum(case when pref_status = 2 then amount end) as npe
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and pref_status in (1, 2)
    group by lei_code
),
joined as (
    select exposure.lei_code, exposure.exposure, loans.loans_gross, loans.npe,
           row_number() over (order by exposure.exposure desc) as size_rank
    from exposure
    inner join loans on loans.lei_code = exposure.lei_code
    where loans.loans_gross > 0
)
select case when size_rank <= 11 then 'largest 11 banks' else 'other banks' end as bank_group,
       count(*) as banks,
       sum(npe) / sum(loans_gross) * 100 as pooled_npe_ratio_pct,
       avg(npe / loans_gross * 100) as simple_average_npe_ratio_pct
from joined
group by 1
union all
select 'correlation: ln(exposure) vs bank NPE ratio', count(*),
       corr(ln(exposure), npe / loans_gross), null
from joined;

queries.question: What is each bank's non-performing exposure ratio? (bank-level version of Q23)
queries.sql:
with bybank as (
    select item, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, credit.lei_code, bank_metadata.name, sum(amount) as bankwise
    from credit
    inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = credit.lei_code
    inner join prefstatus_metadata on prefstatus_metadata.pref_status = credit.pref_status
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and credit.pref_status in ('1', '2')
    group by item, credit.pref_status, prefstatus_metadata.label, credit.lei_code, bank_metadata.name
),
total as (
    select item, lei_code, sum(bankwise) as total
    from bybank
    group by item, lei_code
)
select bybank.item, pref_status, label, bybank.lei_code, name, bankwise, total, ((bankwise / total) * 100) as bank_np_pct
from bybank
inner join total on total.item = bybank.item and total.lei_code = bybank.lei_code
where pref_status = 2
order by bank_np_pct desc;

queries.question: What is each bank's current CET1 capital ratio?
notes: Note: Amount is not in one unit across the oth table. Capital and P&L items (e.g. 2520102, 2520138, 2520335) are in EUR mn; ratio items (2520140, 2520905) are plain decimals (0.13 = 13%). Very high values (Kommuninvest ~352%, Kuntarahoitus ~89%) belong to municipal funding agencies with near-zero risk-weighted assets and are genuine, not data errors.
queries.sql:
select item, label, oth.lei_code, bank_metadata.name, amount
from oth
inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = oth.lei_code
where period = '202506' and item = '2520140'
order by amount;

queries.question: Combine total assets, NPE ratio and CET1 ratio into one reference table (shortlist for the stress test)
queries.result: Combines Q24, Q25 and total assets (item 2521010). Used to shortlist banks for the stress test.
queries.sql:
with t as (
    select distinct oth.item, oth.label, oth.lei_code, bank_metadata.name
    from oth
    inner join bank_metadata on bank_metadata.lei_code = oth.lei_code
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2521010')
),
exposure as (
    select item, lei_code, sum(amount) as exp_total
    from oth
    where period = '202506' and item = '2521010'
    group by item, lei_code
),
prefstatus as (
    select lei_code, sum(amount) as exp_prefstatus
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and pref_status in ('1', '2')
    group by lei_code
),
npe as (
    select lei_code, sum(amount) as npe
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520603' and pref_status = 2
    group by lei_code
),
nperatio as (
    select npe.lei_code, ((npe / exp_prefstatus) * 100) as nperatio
    from npe
    inner join prefstatus on prefstatus.lei_code = npe.lei_code
),
cet1 as (
    select lei_code, amount as cet1ratio
    from oth
    where period = '202506' and item = '2520140'
)
select t.item, label, t.lei_code, name, exp_total, nperatio, cet1ratio
from t
inner join exposure on exposure.item = t.item and exposure.lei_code = t.lei_code
inner join nperatio on nperatio.lei_code = t.lei_code
inner join cet1 on cet1.lei_code = t.lei_code
order by t.item, name;

queries.question: Provision coverage of performing and non-performing loans, per bank
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn | Item(s): 2520603 (gross carrying amount), 2520613 (impairment and provisions)
queries.sql:
with c as (
    select item, pref_status, lei_code, amount
    from credit
    where period = '202506' and item in ('2520603', '2520613') and pref_status in ('1', '2')
),
t as (
    select lei_code,
           sum(case when item = '2520603' and pref_status = 1 then amount else 0 end) as gross_p,
           sum(case when item = '2520613' and pref_status = 1 then amount else 0 end) as provision_p,
           sum(case when item = '2520603' and pref_status = 2 then amount else 0 end) as gross_np,
           sum(case when item = '2520613' and pref_status = 2 then amount else 0 end) as provision_np
    from c
    group by lei_code
)
select t.lei_code, gross_p, provision_p, round((provision_p / nullif(gross_p, 0)) * 100, 3) as coverage_p,
       gross_np, provision_np, round((provision_np / nullif(gross_np, 0)) * 100, 3) as coverage_np
from t;

queries.question: CET1 capital and total risk exposure amount (RWA), per bank
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn | Item(s): 2520102 (CET1 capital), 2520138 (total RWA)
queries.result: Items 2520102 and 2520138, the capital inputs of the stress-test model.
queries.sql:
select item, label, lei_code, amount
from oth
where period = '202506' and item in ('2520102', '2520138')
order by item;

queries.question: One row per stress-model bank with every input the model uses (feeds EBA_stress_test_model.xlsx, sheet Bank Inputs)
queries.meta: Period: 202506 (Jun 2025) | Units: EUR mn; CET1 ratio is a decimal (0.13 = 13%)
notes: Items: 2521010 total assets, 2520138 RWA, 2520102 CET1 capital, 2520140 CET1 ratio, 2520332 profit before tax, 2520333 profit after tax (oth; half-year cumulative, n_quarters = 2); 2520603 gross loans by Perf_Status 1 and 2, 2520613 provisions on non-performing loans (credit, NPE sheet) Kommuninvest is extracted for reference; the model excludes it from the stress run (assumption A16).
queries.result: The output is pasted as values into the Bank Inputs sheet of EBA_stress_test_model.xlsx; the sheet's CET1 ratio check column (CET1 capital ÷ RWA) reproduces the reported ratio for every bank.
queries.sql:
with banks as (
    select lei_code, name
    from bank_metadata
    where lei_code in (
        '5493006QMFDDMYWIAM13', -- Banco Santander
        '529900S9YO2JHTIIDG38', -- BAWAG Group
        'R0MUWSFPU8MPRO8K5P83', -- BNP Paribas
        '2138008AVF4W7FMW8W87', -- CEC Bank
        '851WYGNLUQLFZBSYGB56', -- Commerzbank
        '7LTWFZYICNSX8D621K86', -- Deutsche Bank
        'FR969500TJ5KRTCJQWXH', -- Groupe Credit Agricole
        'F0HUI1NY1AZMJMD8LP67', -- HSBC Continental Europe
        '549300NYKK9MWM7GGW15', -- ING Groep
        'EV2XZWMLLXF2QRX0CD47', -- Kommuninvest (reference only)
        '549300C9KPZR0VZ16R05', -- Morgan Stanley Europe Holding SE
        '485100FX5Y9YLAQLNP12'  -- Revolut Holdings Europe
    )
),
o as (
    select lei_code,
           sum(case when item = 2521010 then amount end) as total_assets,
           sum(case when item = 2520138 then amount end) as rwa,
           sum(case when item = 2520102 then amount end) as cet1_capital,
           sum(case when item = 2520140 then amount end) as cet1_ratio,
           sum(case when item = 2520332 then amount end) as pbt_h1,
           sum(case when item = 2520333 then amount end) as pat_h1
    from oth
    where period = 202506 and item in (2521010, 2520138, 2520102, 2520140, 2520332, 2520333)
    group by lei_code
),
c as (
    select lei_code,
           sum(case when item = 2520603 and pref_status = '1' then amount else 0 end) as performing,
           sum(case when item = 2520603 and pref_status = '2' then amount else 0 end) as non_performing,
           sum(case when item = 2520613 and pref_status = '2' then amount else 0 end) as npe_provisions
    from credit
    where period = 202506 and item in (2520603, 2520613) and pref_status in ('1', '2')
    group by lei_code
)
select banks.lei_code, banks.name,
       o.total_assets, o.rwa, o.cet1_capital, o.cet1_ratio,
       c.performing, c.non_performing, c.npe_provisions,
       o.pbt_h1, o.pat_h1,
       round(c.non_performing / nullif(c.performing + c.non_performing, 0), 6) as npe_ratio,
       round(c.npe_provisions / nullif(c.non_performing, 0), 6) as npe_coverage
from banks
left join o on o.lei_code = banks.lei_code
left join c on c.lei_code = banks.lei_code
order by banks.name;

banks.requirement_basis: FALLBACK: P1 4.50 + P2R(CET1) proxy 1.20 (ECB SSM average) + CCoB 2.50 + CCyB RO 1.00 + O-SII 1.00 + SyRB 2.00 (assumed still applied; last confirmed 2022)
MDA threshold: P1 4.50 + P2R(CET1) 1.27 + CCoB 2.50 + O-SII 1.25 + CCyB 0.66 + SyRB 0.10 + AT1 shortfall 0.04
P1 4.50 + P2R(CET1) 1.63 + CCoB 2.50 + CCyB 0.48 + SyRB 0.13 + max(G-SII 1.50; O-SII 2.00)
P1 4.50 + P2R(CET1) + CCoB 2.50 + G-SIB 1.00 + CCyB ~0.77 + SyRB ~0.05 (P2R 1.80 total)
Stated CET1 requirement excl. P2G (KM1: P2R(CET1) 1.5 + CBR 3.6)
Fully loaded CET1 requirement incl. CCyB 0.94 and P2R 1.65 (total)
